answer: A public audit trail makes each agent's transaction history a shared, tamper-evident record. Because clones spawned from one model share behavioral fingerprints—timing, phrasing, response patterns—auditors can cluster them statistically. A periodic beacon timestamps every action, and any lantern that illuminates a cluster raises the attacker's marginal cost per fake identity: each new sybil must not only pass entry but also diverge from its siblings' recorded traces, or inherit their exposure.
